population: 38 adults in septic shock, 0.026-1.7 mcg/kg/min

blocking_issue: None for the curve.  Fitted in pregnancy; other adults are an extrapolation.  The paper's 24-hour exposure and all six Table 4 maintenance doses are reproduced.

population: 6 healthy volunteers, 0.5 mg/kg IV and 200 mg PO, fasting and fed
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article: non-compartmental (first sample at 15 min, so no distribution phase).  Fasting IV clearance 1923 mL/min, Vz 567 L, half-life 214 min; food raised all three about 20% (not significant) and oral bioavailability from 0.26 to 0.36.  Confirms Kanto 1981's clearance; its half-life (3.6 h) is shorter than Kanto's 4.9 h, as Rubin 1983 and Cheymol 1997 also suggest.
source: Daneshmend TK, Roberts CJ. The influence of food on the oral and intravenous pharmacokinetics of a high clearance drug: a study with labetalol. Br J Clin Pharmacol 1982;14:73-78. PMID 7104169.

population: 10 hypertensive pregnant women, 7 postpartum, 10 controls, 50 mg IV
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article: biexponential fits whose coefficients are not printed; medians CL 1.96-2.35 L/min (24.8-34.8 mL/min/kg), Vss 3.7-6.3 L/kg, half-life 2.1-2.5 h.  An effect compartment was fitted (supine pressure falling 0.38 mmHg per ng/mL in pregnancy) but its keq is not reported.  With Cheymol 1997 it confirms Kanto 1981's clearance and suggests Kanto's Vss (9.0 L/kg) and half-life (4.9 h) run about 1.7 times long.
source: Rubin PC, Butters L, Kelman AW, Fitzsimons C, Reid JL. Labetalol disposition and concentration-effect relationships during pregnancy. Br J Clin Pharmacol 1983;15:465-470. PMID 6849783.

population: 9 obese and 9 normal-weight volunteers; propranolol, labetalol and nebivolol IV
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article: non-compartmental (labetalol controls CL 81.5 L/h, Vss 4.8 L/kg, half-life 4.4 h; propranolol CL 41.6 L/h, Vss 3.1 L/kg, 3.4 h), doses as base per kg of ideal weight.  On the hydrochloride basis it matches Kanto's labetalol clearance (25.2 against 24.8 mL/min/kg) but not its Vss (5.2 against 9.0 L/kg), and Fagan 1982's propranolol per kilogram.  Peak blood-pressure and heart-rate effects at 1-2 h.
source: Cheymol G, Poirier JM, Carrupt PA, et al. Pharmacokinetics of beta-adrenoceptor blockers in obese and normal volunteers. Br J Clin Pharmacol 1997;43:563-570. PMID 9205815.

blocking_issue: Built from the abstract's clearance, central volume and two half-lives; the printed Vss checks it to 2.6%. population: 62 women at caesarean delivery, 0.25 or 0.5 mg IV bolus
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article: medians at 1 and 5 min only (0.5 mg: 80 and 3.2 ng/mL), no model.  They fall 25-30-fold in 4 min, a half-life near 1 min, where the Armstrong model falls 1.6-fold: the library's nitroglycerin is unsuitable for boluses.  The 1-min samples were drawn downstream of the injection and are probably inflated.

population: 10 patients with congestive cardiac failure, 21 mcg/min
blocking_issue: One compartment from the clearance (6.2 L/min) and the time constant of the rise (8.1 min); the supplied full text confirms Teflon tubing (no adsorption) and arterial sampling.  After a stop the measured half-life was 1-3 min, faster than the model's 5.6, so the offset is drawn too slowly.  Healthy volunteers' venous clearance is 3 to 10 times higher (McNiff 1981).
source: Armstrong PW, Watts DG, Moffat JA. Steady state pharmacokinetic haemodynamic studies of intravenous nitroglycerin in congestive cardiac failure. Br J Clin Pharmacol 1983;16:385-390. PMID 6414501.

population: 51 women with preeclampsia, 120 mg/kg over 1 h then 24 mg/kg/h
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article. population: 12 healthy volunteers, 20-min and 24-h infusions
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article. population: 36 healthy volunteers, 18-70 y, 0.04-0.20 mcg/kg/min, awake and anaesthetised

population: 12 septic shock and 11 trauma patients, sedated and ventilated
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article: one compartment, CL = 59 600 / SAPS II mL/min and V 8840 mL (Table 3), which reproduces the paper's three worked clearances and half-lives (SAPS II 20, 30, 66).  Not offered beside Li 2024: SAPS II is not a Patient Profile field, and the dose basis is unstated in a French study, where norepinephrine is often dosed as the tartrate, twice the base.  Clearance at SAPS II 50 is 1.19 L/min, about half the healthy volunteers' 2.1.
source: Beloeil H, Mazoit JX, Benhamou D, Duranteau J. Norepinephrine kinetics and dynamics in septic shock and trauma patients. Br J Anaesth 2005;95:782-788. PMID 16227334.

population: 38 hypotensive critically ill children, 2-85 kg (median 6.7)
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article and supplement (definitions only): one compartment, CL 6.6 L/h x BW^0.75, endogenous production 3.12 mcg/h x BW^0.75, V fixed at the circulating volume 0.08 L/kg (Table 2); it reproduces its own 10 kg example and Figure 8.  A candidate for a paediatric norepinephrine; not offered yet because the dose basis is unstated and the product used (noradrenaline 2 mg/mL, Renaudin) may be labelled as the tartrate, a factor of two.
source: Oualha M, Treluyer JM, Lesage F, et al. Population pharmacokinetics and haemodynamic effects of norepinephrine in hypotensive critically ill children. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2014;78:886-897. PMID 24802558.

population: 29 adults under propofol-remifentanil anaesthesia for neurosurgery, 10 mcg peripheral boluses and infusions
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article and supplement.  Its time to peak effect, 74 s (median, IQR 53-94) for mean arterial pressure after a 10 mcg bolus (heart rate 74 s, cardiac output 61 s), is the implemented norepinephrine's effect site.  Its PK is not used: two compartments with a 25 s lag and a depot whose output takes a nonlinear power (beta 1.21) of the amount, V1 0.49 L, k10 0.05, k12 0.06, k21 0.04 /s; PD a direct Emax on plasma (E0 57.1, Emax 113.5 mmHg, EC50 15.7 nmol/L, gamma 1.46) or a Windkessel model for the undershoot after a bolus.
source: Joachim J, Cartailler J, Vallee F, et al. Design of a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model for administration of low dose peripheral norepinephrine during general anaesthesia. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2024;90:2861-2869. PMID 39039779.

population: pooled children and 4 adult volunteers given IV
blocking_issue: An alternative to the implemented Hengstmann 1982 model.  The abstract prints a complete two-compartment set (CL 160 L/h, V1 13.3 L, Q 25.3 L/h, V2 225 L at 70 kg) but labels it for the nasal formulation, prints no allometric exponents or dose basis, and its 7-hour terminal half-life differs from Hengstmann's 2-3 h.
to_obtain: Anderson BJ et al. The phenylephrine concentration-response relationship for blood pressure after nasal delivery. Paediatr Anaesth 2017;27:1050-1055. PMID 28868789, doi 10.1111/pan.13221 (optional now).
source: Anderson BJ et al. Paediatr Anaesth 2017;27:1050-1055. PMID 28868789.

population: 4 healthy volunteers, 0.84 mg 3H-phenylephrine IV over 12.5-20 min
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article.  Two compartments, the mean of the four subjects' fits in Table 3, which reproduces the paper's mean CL (2095 mL/min) and Vdss (340 L); the end-of-infusion concentration matches Table 2.  The abstract's 'CL 2 l/h' is the misprint it looked like (2 L/min).  Dose basis unstated (hydrochloride assumed, as labelled; 22% if wrong).

population: 9 healthy men, 10 then 3 mcg/kg/min
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article.  Table 4's micro constants reproduce every derived value and Equation 3's 3.77 steady-state constant.  The 0.5 min lag and the endogenous baseline are not represented; concentrations at the same rate varied 10- to 75-fold, and the model overpredicted the 10 mcg/kg/min infusion.  Dose basis unstated (hydrochloride assumed).
source: MacGregor DA, Smith TE, Prielipp RC, et al. Pharmacokinetics of dopamine in healthy male subjects. Anesthesiology 2000;92:338-346. PMID 10691218.

population: critically ill adults, 3 and 6 mcg/kg/min
blocking_issue: CL, Vss and the terminal half-life only (underdetermined), and Vss and half-life roughly double between the two rates, so the kinetics are dose-dependent.

source: Le Corre P et al. Crit Care Med 1993;21:1652-1657. PMID 8222680.

population: 7 healthy men, 30-min infusions of 70-280 mcg/kg
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article.  Two compartments per kg from Table I's means (CL 0.920, V 0.291, Vss 1.13, distribution clearance 0.826 L/h/kg).  The unlabelled row identified as the distribution clearance reproduces all seven subjects' printed distribution times; V = CL x MRT and Vss = CL x MRT check every subject once subject 3's clearance is read as 0.883 (printed 0.833, a transposition: 0.883 also makes the mean the printed 0.920).  Clearance at the fast end of the published range (0.31-0.91 L/h/kg).
source: Modi NB, Veng-Pedersen P, Graham DJ, Dow RJ. Application of a system analysis approach to population pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of nicardipine hydrochloride in healthy males. J Pharm Sci 1993;82:705-713. PMID 8360844.

population: 5 healthy men, 5 mg/h for 3 h
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article.  Two compartments per subject (Table 1 means: CL 8.23 mL/min/kg, alpha 3.42 and beta 0.200 /h, Vc 20.6 L, terminal half-life 4 h 45 min).  From the means at 70 kg: CL 34.6 L/h, V2 77.5 L, Vss 1.40 L/kg; half the clearance of Modi 1993, the implemented model, so at 5 mg/h it predicts 145 ng/mL against Modi's 78 (the dose was chosen to give about 100).
source: Graham DJM, Dow RJ, Hall DJ, Alexander OF, Mroszczak EJ, Freedman D. The metabolism and pharmacokinetics of nicardipine hydrochloride in man. Br J Clin Pharmacol 1985;20 Suppl 1:23S-28S. PMID 4027149.

population: 40 adults undergoing cardiac surgery, boluses 0.25-2 mg
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article: Table 2 is not a coherent two-compartment model.  Its 'redistribution half-time' is ln2 Vc/CL (3.5 min at 1 mg exactly), not an independent rate; Varea is 1.3-2.2 times smaller than CL/beta in every group; the central volumes (0.02-0.12 L/kg) are below plasma volume, the bolus having gone into the right atrium and the samples drawn from the pulmonary artery; clearance doubles across the dose groups; and sampling stopped at 4 h.
source: Cheung AT, Guvakov DV, Weiss SJ, Savino JS, Salgo IS, Meng QC. Nicardipine intravenous bolus dosing for acutely decreasing arterial blood pressure during general anesthesia for cardiac operations. Anesth Analg 1999;89:1116-1123. PMID 10553821.

Its Table 1 lists the intravenous studies a compartmental model would come from (Campbell 1985, Graham 1985, Wagner 1987, Hirota 1998, Rocha 1990, Modi 1993).

blocking_issue: Three compartments (CL about 800 mL/min, Vd about 1 L/kg, terminal half-life 4-5 h) without a printed volume and clearance set.

source: Guerret M et al. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 1989;37:381-385. PMID 2598970.

population: 16 healthy volunteers, 50 mg IV over 9.5 min and 500 mg oral
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article: non-compartmental only (AUC, Cmax, terminal half-life 18.5 h, range 7.7-48).  The plasma curve is clearly multiphasic, so a one-compartment model from CL and the half-life would misplace the early concentrations badly; no compartmental parameters are reported.  A three-compartment adult population model is reported in the EMA ProveBlue assessment.
to_obtain: EMA ProveBlue (methylthioninium chloride) Article 46 assessment report P46-010; FDA ProvayBlue NDA 204630 clinical pharmacology review (a population model on a modern assay would settle the tenfold conflict with Peter 2000).
source: Walter-Sack I, Rengelshausen J, Oberwittler H, et al. High absolute bioavailability of methylene blue given as an aqueous oral formulation. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 2009;65:179-189. PMID 18810398.

population: 7 healthy volunteers, 100 mg IV over 30 s
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article: a complete triexponential fit to the pooled data, C = 9.4 exp(-0.237 t) + 3.8 exp(-0.065 t) + 0.3 exp(-0.0022 t) umol/L, which would fix three compartments.  But its AUC per mg is about a tenth of Walter-Sack 2009's LC-MS/MS measurements (1250 against about 12 900 ng h/mL per 100 mg in whole blood), whose authors suggest earlier assays measured only unbound drug; and its terminal phase is extrapolated from 4 h of sampling.  The two sources cannot both be right, and neither alone is a defensible model.
source: Peter C, Hongwan D, Kupfer A, Lauterburg BH. Pharmacokinetics and organ distribution of intravenous and oral methylene blue. Eur J Clin Pharmacol 2000;56:247-250. PMID 10952480.

population: 3 healthy men, 1.35 and 2.15 mg (6 experiments)
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article (and Part II, its pharmacodynamics).  Built from Table I's V_P, CL, k_PT and k_TP; Vdss, alpha, the terminal half-life and Vd_ps check it within 4%.  Doses are the base in the source and the sulfate as labelled.  Three young men; distribution was dose-dependent; age and urine flow are not covariates.  The effect site peaks 1.5 min after a bolus, the clinical time to peak heart rate (S. L. Shafer); Part II's peripheral-amount link and Scheinin 1999's ke0 were set aside as slower than that.
source: Hinderling PH, Gundert-Remy U, Schmidlin O. Integrated pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of atropine in healthy humans. I: Pharmacokinetics. J Pharm Sci 1985;74:703-710. PMID 4032240; II: Pharmacodynamics, 711-717, PMID 4032241.

population: 8 healthy volunteers, 10 mcg/kg IV (with glycopyrrolate and scopolamine sessions)
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article.  Two compartments by PCNONLIN (V_c 1.31 L/kg, CL 1.74 L/h, half-lives 4.5 min and 1.89 h, as printed) and an effect compartment on the Hayano index of heart-rate variability: ke0 11.0 /h (equilibration half-time 4.7 min), EC50 1.35 ng/mL, gamma 6.07.  Not used for the effect site: with Hinderling's plasma curve its ke0 puts the peak at 3.2 min, twice the clinical 90 s, and its endpoint is heart-rate variability, not heart rate (which peaked at its 10-min sample).  A radioreceptor assay measures the active l-hyoscyamine.
source: Scheinin H, Helminen A, Huhtala S, et al. Spectral analysis of heart rate variability as a quantitative measure of parasympatholytic effect: integrated pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of three anticholinergic drugs. Ther Drug Monit 1999;21:141-151. PMID 10217331.

population: 105 adults with acute atrial fibrillation given IV digoxin (DAAF trial)
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article. population: re-analysis of 12 healthy men given 1 mg IV (Kramer 1979) and a concentration-clamp study
blocking_issue: Read from the supplied article: a pharmacodynamic model on Kramer 1979's plasma curve, not a PK model. So digoxinIV's 87-min effect site (Hornestam 2003) stands for rate control, not inotropy.
source: Weiss M, Kang W. Inotropic effect of digoxin in humans: mechanistic pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic model based on slow receptor binding. Pharm Res 2004;21:231-236. PMID 15032303.
